title: Introduce contingency fuse and progressive evacuation safeguard (hotfix)
author: Maya Chen
description:
Background: During a regional capacity spike we observed a pattern where long-running slowpaths caused connection pileups and aggressive tenant eviction, leading to cascading SLO drops for mid-tier customers. This PR implements a compact "contingency fuse" in the serving runtime and a progressive evacuation safeguard at the routing layer to reduce oscillation and allow graceful degradation under transient overload.
Motivation: Existing circuit breakers flipped aggressively when downstream kv pressure rose; that behavior is correct for severe faults but caused unnecessary tenant reinstates and noisy metrics during short-lived surges. The contingency fuse is a lightweight short-window gate that combines health signals (local latency quantiles + kv pressure) to temporarily divert traffic to standby routes before full eviction. The progressive evacuation safeguard introduces a staged drain with time-decayed backoff so tenants are not immediately evicted for brief infra perturbations.
Key changes: 1) runtime/evacuator/contingency_fuse.go — new fuse with configurable thresholds and exponential cooloff. 2) routing/fallback_policy.go — staged evacuation orchestration and fallback scorer adjustments. 3) controller/telemetry/evac_metrics.go — new metrics and tags for contingency decisions. 4) deploy/hotfix-release.yaml — rollout config with 5% canary and 10m observation window. 5) tests/integration/evacuation_sim_test.go — deterministic scenarios that simulate kv pressure spikes, short surges, and regional failover.
Design notes:
- Fuse window is intentionally short (250ms sampling) to catch fast surges without impacting steady-state.
- Fuse decision is a composite: p90 latency > X AND kv_queue_ratio > Y; both thresholds are configurable per-region and per-tier.
- Progressive evacuation uses three phases: warn (no eviction, ramp weights), partial-evac (soft-evict lowest priority), full-evac (hard-evict). Each phase has decaying TTLs to allow automatic healing.
- Telemetry includes decision_reason tag to help correlate fuse hits with SLO deltas.
Testing and validation: Unit tests cover decision logic and backoff; integration harness runs a 2-hour simulated surge that previously repro'd the incident and shows reduced eviction events by ~72% while SLO hit rate improved 48% in the mid-tier cohort.
CI: initial run showed a flaky integration test (timeout), fixed by tightening wait conditions; full CI green on rerun.
Rollout plan: Canary 5% across two low-risk regions for 30 minutes, observe contingency_fuse.hit_rate, tenant_evictions, and p95 latency regressions. If metrics stable, ramp to 50% over 2 hours, then full rollout.
Rollback: feature flags gate fuse and progressive evacuation separately; revert the feature flag to disable behaviors without code rollback.
Related: linear ENG-2148 captures the incident timeline; SUP-9123 includes customer reports.
Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration simulation added
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards updated
- [x] Rollout plan + feature flagging
- [x] Postmortem link prepared (internal)
Migration/compatibility: Default thresholds are conservative; no customer-visible config changes required.
Hotfix notes: Backported a minimal patch to the 2026-02-15 maintenance branch to stop immediate re-evictions in the middle of the previous incident.
Ops: On-call runbook updated with a short playbook to toggle the contingency fuse and sequence rollback.
